endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Make notification of material changes a contractual obligation at procurement, rather than relying on vendor goodwill.

endorsements.title: Considerations for the regulation of generative AI-enabled medical devices (discussion paper)
endorsements.quote: This element also considers accurate tool use and recognition of erroneous tool outputs, compliance with human-oversight checkpoints before irreversible or high-consequence actions, graceful handling of tool failures, and resistance to prompt injection through user inputs, retrieved content, and tool outputs.

endorsements.title: Clinical Artificial Intelligence (AI) Liability in the MENA Region: a Comparative Analysis of Hospital, Physician, Suppliers, and Vendor Responsibility
endorsements.quote: vendors and suppliers should contractually commit to validated performance claims, secure-by-design engineering, version control, timely patching and update/change-control procedures, post-market surveillance with shared incident reporting and root-cause analysis, and clear allocation of responsibilities for data quality versus model performance

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied tests whether contractual change-notice, documentation, and local review requirements reduce harm from silent vendor model changes, and no study documents the hazard itself. Three sources endorse the practice, one of them as a must, but the support rests on expert and regulatory judgment rather than measured outcomes.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies that test the practice and zero studies that document the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The three endorsements come from a playbook, a regulatory discussion paper, and a commentary, and they represent expert opinion rather than comparative data.

The CHAI playbook states that change notification should be a contractual obligation at procurement, not a matter of vendor goodwill. A MENA liability commentary recommends vendor commitments to version control and update and change-control procedures. The generative AI device discussion paper describes oversight checkpoints but does not directly address contract terms. None of these sources reports tested effects.

commentary.research_gap: No study measures how often vendor model updates, retraining, upstream changes, or newly activated AI features occur without customer awareness, or whether contract clauses requiring advance notice and local review change detection rates, performance drift, or patient harm. Studies could compare organizations with and without such clauses on time to detect model changes and on post-update performance.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice in any population, so there is no evidence on Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy settings. Safety-net systems may hold less contract bargaining power with vendors, and it remains unknown whether this practice is feasible or effective for them.
